land.text: the County of Maine 'returning the county to the crown' in 1481

capitals.name: Le Mans
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Le Mans, the former county's capital'.

correction.text: the Cliopatria shape unchanged but holding only to 1050: 'Count Geoffrey's taking possession of the city of Mans (shortly after 26 March 1051)'; from 1051 the county is Angevin

keyframe_review.note: 13,553 km2 (bbox 1.2 W to 1.3 E, 47.5-48.5 N). The Maine page gives no area; the gazetteer's own region 'Maine (France)' is 11,886 km2, within 14%, so the outline is sane. Years: Hugh III (c. 991-c. 1015) 'was forced to recognize Fulk III, Count of Anjou as his overlord' (Maine page), so even before 1051 the county is an Angevin vassal (to be recorded in the county-of-anjou dossier). Cliopatria keeps the shape to 1055 and has nothing for 1056-1065; the Maine page also dates Geoffrey Martel's invasion of Le Mans to 1056, but its own text calls 1051 'clear'.

correction.text: the 1066 shape, from the date William 'controlled the county by the beginning of 1064'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no shape for 1056-1065. William of Normandy 'invaded Maine in force in 1063' against Fulk IV of Anjou and controlled the county by the beginning of 1064, as heir of Herbert (who died childless in 1062) and for Margaret, betrothed to Robert Curthose.

13,553 km2, the same outline. The pages show a county that is Norman only until 1070 ('the Normans were expelled in 1070, and young Hugh V was proclaimed Count of Maine'), held by Hugh V and then Elias I (1092) against Norman attacks in 1073, 1088, 1098 and 1099, and taken by Fulk V of Anjou in 1110; Cliopatria's umbrella link to (Kingdom of England) for 1066-1146 is therefore doubtful after 1070 (a question for the kingdom-of-england dossier). Shape kept: no page gives a different outline.

13,553 km2, the same outline once more. The English occupation began after Verneuil in 1424; 'The English held Le Mans until 1448 and Fresnay until 1449', so the county is whole again in 1450. Cliopatria has no Maine shape for 1111-1449: the land is inside the Anjou, Angevin Empire, France and Valois-Anjou shapes (ledger 1110).
13,553 km2, unchanged; 1453 is only the end of the Hundred Years' War elsewhere. No page opened dates a Maine border move in 1453-1474.

13,553 km2, unchanged. Charles IV 'succeeded his father as Count of Maine, Guise, Mortain and Gien in 1472', became Duke of Anjou and Count of Provence in 1480 and died on 10 December 1481 after willing his domains to Louis XI.

region.text: the county of Le Mans, which Hugh III held as a vassal of Fulk III of Anjou

ledger.note: 990: the County of Maine, at Le Mans, enters the record; Hugh III (c. 991-c. 1015) 'was forced to recognize Fulk III, Count of Anjou as his overlord'. Page silent on the county's origin: 990 is Cliopatria's first year for the row.

region.text: the County of Maine under Hugh IV, taken by Geoffrey Martel

ledger.note: 1051: Geoffrey Martel of Anjou takes Le Mans. 'Count Geoffrey's taking possession of the city of Mans (shortly after 26 March 1051)'; 'in 1051 Hugh IV died and the citizens of Le Mans opened their gate to the Angevins' (Maine page). Hugh IV's son Herbert II fled to the Norman court; the Maine page dates Geoffrey's invasion of Le Mans to 1056.

region.text: the County of Maine, claimed by William for Margaret

ledger.note: 1063: William of Normandy invades Maine. 'William invaded Maine in force in 1063' despite 'stiff opposition from Fulk IV, Count of Anjou', claiming it for Herbert's sister Margaret, betrothed to Robert Curthose; Herbert had died childless in 1062 naming William his successor.
1064: William holds Maine. 'he controlled the county by the beginning of 1064.'

region.text: the County of Maine, controlled by William by the beginning of 1064

ledger.note: 1064: Maine passes from the Angevins to William of Normandy as count.

1070: Le Mans throws out the Normans. 'In 1069 the citizens of Le Mans revolted against the Normans'; 'the Normans were expelled in 1070, and young Hugh V was proclaimed Count of Maine.' Same county, a native count again.

1092: Hugh V sells Maine to his cousin Elias I of La Flèche. Hugh 'sold it to Elias for 10,000 shillings in 1092'; Elias was captured by William Rufus on 28 April 1098, besieged Le Mans in 1099 and took it from the Norman garrison in 1100.

region.text: the County of Maine, passing to Eremburga and Fulk V of Anjou

ledger.note: 1110: Fulk V of Anjou takes Maine. Elias died on 11 July 1110 and 'the county of Maine passed to his daughter Eremburga and her husband, Fulk V of Anjou'; 'Fulk V ... took Maine over in 1110' (Maine page). From here Maine is Angevin (Anjou 1110-1151, Angevin Empire 1152-1204, then Philip II: 'the French seneschal William des Roches took Touraine, Anjou and Maine on behalf of the French king' in the war that ended in 1204).

region.text: Le Mans, held by the English until 1448, and Fresnay, until 1449

ledger.note: 1449: the English leave the county. After Verneuil in 1424 'the English occupied Maine, and John of Lancaster took the title of Duke'; 'The English held Le Mans until 1448 and Fresnay until 1449.' The county is drawn again from Cliopatria's 1450 shape. Between 1110 and 1424 the land lay inside Anjou, the Angevin Empire and France (the Count of Maine was a peer of the realm from 1331).

region.text: the County of Maine, returned to the crown

ledger.note: 1481: Charles IV of Anjou, Count of Maine since 1472, dies on 10 December and his domains pass to Louis XI. 'He willed his domains to his cousin, king Louis XI of France'; 'Charles IV, Duke of Anjou bequeathed his lands to Louis XI of France, thus returning the county to the crown' (Maine page).

wars.name: Norman conquest of Maine
wars.outcome: William of Normandy invaded Maine in 1063 against Fulk IV of Anjou and controlled the county by the beginning of 1064.

wars.name: Norman attacks on Maine
wars.outcome: After the Le Mans revolt of 1069 and the expulsion of 1070, Norman attacks came in 1073, 1088, 1098 and 1099; Elias I was captured on 28 April 1098, besieged Le Mans in 1099 and with Fulk expelled the Norman garrison in 1100. The county stayed independent to 1110.
wars.note: No border moved in these years on any page opened, so no contest zone is drawn.

wars.name: English occupation of Maine

zones.text: Maine: Le Mans to 1448, Fresnay to 1449

wars.outcome: After Verneuil (1424) the English occupied Maine and John of Lancaster took the ducal title; they held Le Mans until 1448 and Fresnay until 1449.
wars.note: Cliopatria draws no separate Maine shape in these years; the occupation is not drawn as an occupation event for that reason.

wars.name: Geoffrey Martel's war over Maine
wars.outcome: Geoffrey Martel took Mans in 1051; 'For the next several years, the war was centered in the County of Maine, with Duke William on the offensive', and he kept resisting in Maine until his death on 14 November 1060.
wars.note: The page dates no campaign in Maine besides 1051, so no contest zone is drawn between 1051 and 1063.

certainty.note: A feudal county drawn from Cliopatria's single outline; no page gives a boundary line.

notes:
Cliopatria draws the County of Maine in 990-1055, 1066-1110 and 1450-1481 only. In 1056-1065 the land is Angevin then Norman, in 1111-1449 it lies inside Anjou, the Angevin Empire, France and Valois-Anjou. The ledger records the hand-overs with those states as counterparts (anjou 1051 and 1110, England 1449) and adds a new keyframe for 1064-1065 (William's control from the beginning of 1064); it does not invent a Maine shape for 1111-1449, so the state has no drawn land in the gap, as with the duchy-of-aquitaine dossier in 1138-1203.
Not modelled: the overlordship of Anjou from c. 991 (Hugh III 'forced to recognize Fulk III ... as his overlord'): a vassal_start belongs in the county-of-anjou dossier (counterpart county-of-maine, 991-1050); the apanage status of the Count of Maine from the 13th century to 1472 (the Maine page names no holders besides the 1331 peerage and Charles IV); the 1056 invasion of Le Mans which the Maine page dates five years after the 1051 taking. Cliopatria's umbrella link of Maine to (Kingdom of England) for 1066-1146 is contradicted by the pages for 1070-1110 (see the _1066 verdict).
Page budget: four pages were opened (limit five). Rulers are omitted: no complete list of counts was opened.
